description: platformAutomerge MUST stay false: a ruleset bypass keys on the actor that PERFORMS the merge, and
GitHub-native auto-merge does not carry it. The pr-approval ruleset arriving
on master grants bypass to the renovate App as an Integration actor,
so renovate has to merge through its own API call -- as the App the bypass
names -- or its green batch sits waiting for a human approval that the
bypass was supposed to make unnecessary.
baseBranches lists both lines: master is v1, main is v2. Renovate counts branches and pull requests
across the whole repository, not per base branch, and each base branch gets its own set of renovate/*
branches (batch, lock file maintenance, majors), so adding main doubles the demand on the default limit
of 10 and a full limit silently starves lock file maintenance (branch-limit-reached). Both limits are 20.
go.sum is written by `go mod tidy`, not by `go get`. Without gomodTidy renovate
adds the new version's hashes and leaves the old ones, and every recipe here
runs `just deps` -> `tidy` first, so every one of them rewrote go.sum and the
shared CI failed it as 'modified the working tree': #127 (github.com/truvity/audit
v0.2.5 -> v0.3.1) sat red on build, test, lint, ts, console and vuln for that
reason alone, holding back the ci-workflows pins that deliver this repository's
own security gate.
gomodTidy tidies only the module whose go.mod renovate edited. This repository has seven
Go modules and most of them replace one another with a path, so one bump moves the go.sum of
modules renovate never touched: #759 left five of them untidy (stale hashes kept, new ones
missing) and failed the check, console and audit e2e jobs until it was redone by hand (#1084).
hack/tidy-modules.sh runs `go mod tidy` in every module, dependencies first, after renovate's
own pass, once per branch. The command is allowlisted by the caller's `allowed-commands`
(truvity/ci-caller, renovate-public.yaml); without that entry renovate refuses it and reports
an artifact error on the pull request.
third_party/ holds patched copies of other projects' modules, kept as
upstream wrote them at one version. Their go.mod files are upstream's and
are not updated here; the root go.mod's require is.
The root go.mod replaces github.com/zitadel/oidc/v3 v3.51.16 with
third_party/zitadel-oidc, a copy with one line removed. A bump leaves the
versioned replace behind and the ID token tests fail. So it gets its own PR,
never the automerged batch, which it would hold red, and a human re-applies
the patch or drops the copy (third_party/zitadel-oidc/README.md).
Drop the copy only after a zitadel/oidc release contains #1021 (issue #1020) or an equivalent fix: dropping it earlier brings the conformance warning back.
prBodyNotes: sluis builds a patched copy of this module (third_party/zitadel-oidc). Re-apply the patch to the new version, or drop the copy if upstream has fixed it: see third_party/zitadel-oidc/README.md.

packageRules.description: MkDocs 2.0 breaks the plugins and theme overrides the documentation site (mkdocs.yaml, hack/mkdocs_hooks.py) is built with; hold it below 2 until they are ported.

The go directive is OWNED by devbox-update (ci-workflows v2.10.0): it aligns go.mod to the toolchain triple in the same PR as devbox.lock — language minor capped by golangci-lint's build Go, patch = the newest release of that line, never downward. Renovate leaves `go` alone so the three can never disagree (2026-08-23; replaces the bump rule and the minor/strict gates that papered over split ownership).

description: Branch `main` is v2 (Go, Rust, Astro and Starlight under site/); `master` is v1. This file is read from
the default branch, so a rule that holds for one line only says so with matchBaseBranches. On main the
managers are gomod (one module), cargo (one workspace), npm (site/, Yarn), devbox and github-actions;
the preset's grouping (all non-major in one PR, after three days), 0.x minors, majors by estate decision
and the weekly lock file maintenance apply as on master. The one difference is automerge: v2 is merged by
the maintainer (GOVERNANCE.md), so Renovate opens the pull requests on main and does not merge them (security fixes keep the preset's automerge).
To let it, delete this rule once the `checks` job has been green on a few of them.
